defects.description: The digits are extracted with `divmod(decimal, 8)` instead of `divmod(decimal, 16)`, so it converts to base 8 rather than hexadecimal.
paraphrases: Dividing by 8 produces octal-style digits, not hex.
The radix is wrong (8 instead of 16), so decimal_to_hexadecimal(255) is not '0xff'.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `divmod(decimal, 16)`. Real (wrong base), findable via the docstring, distinct.

defects.description: New digits are appended (`hexadecimal + values[remainder]`) instead of prepended (`values[remainder] + hexadecimal`), so the hex digits come out in reverse order.
paraphrases: The concatenation order is reversed; it should be `values[remainder] + hexadecimal`.
Digits are produced least-significant first, so appending reverses them.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `values[remainder] + hexadecimal`. Real (digits reversed), findable via the docstring, distinct from the base defect.

defects.description: For negative inputs the value is multiplied by 1 (`decimal *= 1`) rather than -1, so it is never made positive and the while loop produces no digits.
paraphrases: `decimal *= 1` should be `decimal *= -1`; the sign is never flipped.
Negative inputs stay negative, so the loop emits nothing and the digits are lost.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `decimal *= -1`. Real (negatives lose their digits), findable via the -256 docstring example, distinct.
